scope: Corollary 2.6 (Counting heavy boxes) of the manuscript “Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere” (preprints/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 077 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 669efdbef9150144), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose the hypotheses of Lemma 2.5 hold in every time bin with the same H. Fix radii L, w, and use an orientation grid of spacing comparable to ρ = w/L, with translated grids having bounded overlap at each orientation. Let H be the family of boxes of mass at least HW(E)M−e. Then, over all time bins, #H ≤ HW(E) −1 MOκ(e)+o(1) . (2.6)
